results.title: Scientist Personality: Traits, Types, and Career Impact
results.content: Scientist Personality: Traits, Types, and Career Implications. Curiosity and logic may be the hallmarks of scientific thinking, but the minds behind groundbreaking discoveries are far more diverse and complex than the stereotypical lab-coat-wearing genius. The world of science is populated by a rich tapestry of personalities, each contributing their unique strengths and perspectives to the pursuit of knowledge. From the meticulous data analyst to the visionary theorist, the realm of scientific inquiry embraces a wide spectrum of intellectual and emotional traits. The investigative personality that drives scientific progress is a multifaceted gem, reflecting different facets depending on the individual and their chosen field of study. ## Unraveling the Scientist Personality: A Tapestry of Traits. This curious personality is the engine that propels scientific inquiry forward, constantly asking “why” and “how” in the face of the unknown. It’s this relentless pursuit of understanding that has led to some of humanity’s greatest discoveries and innovations.

Title: Four personality traits ECRs can foster to help impact policy and practice - Research to Action
# Four personality traits ECRs can foster to help impact policy and practice. Researchers seeking to translate their work into ‘impact’ – that is, any of the range of positive, tangible influences on society possible through research – are often advised to develop a range of ‘soft’ skills that can help them to navigate the spaces between science, policy, and practice. These include communication skills (social media, public speaking, popular articles), the ability to network effectively with diverse stakeholders, and inside knowledge gained from working in government and industry can all be incredibly useful for impact work. One of the most important attributes of individuals who successfully influence policy and practice is that of honesty – a necessary precondition to building trust with the various actors that you are seeking to influence. We suggest that scientists seeking to impact on policy and practice follow **Pielke Jr’s description of an honest broker**, whereby you present the full suite of available options and perspectives that are available to inform the decision-making process. Humility is an essential precondition of meaningful engagement and trust building, which underpins impact on policy and practice. Finally, and perhaps most importantly, achieving real-world impact requires **resilience.** Your pathway to impact will include a range of challenges, failures, and individuals who will make you doubt yourself, your ability, and even the value of your goals themselves. Working to achieve policy impact in science is hard, and **especially so for early-career researchers (ECRs)**. Make time to celebrate the small wins, no matter how small they are (e.g. developing a research impact plan, establishing a new relationship, etc.). results.title: The changing rationalities of Australian federal and national inclusive education policies | The Australian Educational Researcher | Springer Nature Link
results.content: # The changing rationalities of Australian federal and national inclusive education policies. Ideas and practices associated with inclusive education have featured prominently in the policies and reforms of successive Australian federal governments since the 1990s, yet there are limited historical analyses of these developments. This paper analyses federal and national inclusive education policies in Australia spanning from 1992 to the present. Three distinct phases of policy development are identified, which we suggest are characterised by three dominant rationalities: (1) standardisation, (2) the neo-social and (3) personalisation. In this article, we examine the development of inclusive education policies by Australian federal governments over the last 30 years, with a specific focus on policies relating to disabilities. It is pertinent to focus on the development of inclusive education policies at the federal level because while successive Australian federal governments have played leading roles in driving national reform to the education of students with disability, few studies have been completed that provide historical and conceptual accounts of these developments.

Thus, it is regarded as an educational philosophy. Essentialism as a philosophy has impact on our differentiation or unification ways while addressing. This paper seeks to present how essentialism is used as the basis of our daily communication and its role in our discriminating and unifying efforts in social, cultural and scientific domains. Essentialism in education asserts that common and essential ideas and skills belonging to a certain culture should be taught to all citizens at the same level at especially primary school level.
